'''''Pilularia globulifera''''', or '''pillwort''',<ref name=BSBI07>{{BSBI 2007 |accessdate=2014-10-17 }}</ref> is an unusual species of [[fern]] in the family Marsileaceae. It is native to western Europe,<ref name="iucn status 12 November 2021" /> where it grows at the edges of lakes, ponds, ditches and marshes, on wet clay or clay-sand soil, sometimes in water up to {{convert|30|cm|in|abbr=on}} deep.<ref name=BSBI/>

== Description ==
Pillwort has slender, cylindrical, rush-like fronds up to {{convert|8|cm|in|abbr=on}} tall that are shaped like croziers as they unfurl.<ref name=BSBI>{{cite web |url=http://sppaccounts.bsbi.org/content/pilularia-globulifera-0.html |title=''Pilularia globulifera'' |author=Lockton, A.J. |work=BSBI Species account |publisher=Botanical Society of the British Isles |access-date=12 April 2020}}</ref> 
It has a pea-shaped, 4-chambered [[Sporocarp (ferns)|sporocarp]] about {{convert|3|mm|in|1|abbr=on}} in diameter, each chamber formed from a modified leaf and containing several [[sorus|sori]] bearing both [[megasporangia]] and [[microsporangia]]. The species is thus [[heterosporous]].{{Citation needed|date=May 2021}}

== Habitat ==
Pillwort grows on silt and mud at the margins of lakes, ponds and other watercourses that are submerged for at least part of the year.<ref name=Stace>{{cite book|last=Stace|first=C. A.|author-link = Stace, C. A.|year=2010|title=New Flora of the British Isles|edition=Third|publisher=Cambridge University Press|location = Cambridge, U.K.| isbn=978-0-521-70772-5}}</ref>{{rp|16}} Some of the plants growing in association with this species in the UK include water celery (''[[Apium inundatum]]''), marsh pennywort (''[[Hydrocotyle vulgaris]]'') and lesser spearwort (''[[Ranunculus flammula]]''). In its habitat in shallow water on pond margins or in poached{{clarify|reason=what is the meaning of "poached" in this context|date=April 2020}} wet grassland, it seems to grow well in bare locations where it faces little competition. Populations vary greatly from year to year; it sometimes "disappears" from a site only to recur there many years later, and cleaning out a ditch may stimulate it to reappear.<ref name=BSBI/>

== Distribution ==
This is a rare species, declining as its wetland habitats are reduced by eutrophication and drainage, but is regarded as of least concern by the [[IUCN Red List]]. It is listed on Schedule 8 of the Wildlife (Northern Ireland) Order 1985, but it has not been seen there since 1970 and may now be extinct in the province. It is protected under the [[Wildlife and Countryside Act 1981]] in the rest of the UK, where it is now classified as vulnerable. It is listed as threatened or endangered in nearly all the countries in which it grows.<ref name="iucn status 12 November 2021" />

== Uses ==
Pillwort can be grown in a "bog garden" or as a marginal aquatic in a garden pond.<ref name="iucn status 12 November 2021" />
